newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom Malaysia, SBC link on SAfrica bid.
newsitem.headline: Telekom Malaysia, SBC link on SAfrica bid.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd has joined with SBC Communications Inc to submit a joint bid for the partial privatisation of South Africa's state-run Telkom, South Africa's Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting, Jay Naidoo was quoted as saying.

Both companies have been shortlisted, along with Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom, in the South Africa's government's planned sale of up to 30 percent of Telkom, the world's 28th largest telecommunications operator.

"The deal is lucrative, for the successful bidder can participate in the biggest expansion of telecommunications facility and services ever undertaken in the African continent," national news agency Bernama quoted Naidoo as saying in an interview on a visit to Kuala Lumpur.

"It is worth billions of ringgit, for we are looking at network expansion including increasing lines to the rural areas, training, as well as ways to surf the Internet through the provision of multimedia services," he said.
South Africa, which has a population exceeding 42 million, has only one line per 8.5 persons, he said.
Naidoo, who earlier met Information Minister Mohamed Rahmat, said South Africa's cabinet was currently considering the various potential partners and a decision is expected by next April.
Separately, industry sources in South Africa said Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom were widely expected to join forces to form a rival consortium.
The sale of shares in Telkom is the first major step in South Africa's cautious privatisation programme.
Naidoo arrived here on Sunday for a four-day working visit. He met senior officials at Telekom Malaysia on Monday.
He said South Africa could learn a lot from Malaysia's success in privatisation. Telekom Malaysia was privatised through a listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
